clue.text: Author and director of his alarming fantasy, say

indicators.note: say signals that the director's surname is only heard, not spelt, here

parts.note: Orson Welles directed the alarming 1938 radio version of The War of the Worlds

explanation.surface: A writer and the man who staged his frightening story are named together.
explanation.walkthrough: H G Wells wrote The War of the Worlds; Orson Welles's radio version of it famously panicked listeners. The two surnames sound identical, and 'his' points back to the author.
explanation.definitionFit: H G Wells is a famous English novelist, a straightforward example of an author.

clue.text: Labour fanatic

parts.note: reads as a zealous supporter of the Labour Party, but means someone obsessed with labour in the sense of work

explanation.definitionFit: Someone compulsively devoted to work is a fanatic for labour, read with a small l.

clue.text: Top hat

definitions.meaning: a top is a cover or cap on a container

explanation.definitionFit: A lid is both a cover on top of a pot and, in slang, a hat worn on the head.

clue.text: Writer succeeded with translation to English

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
a crib is a literal translation used by students

explanation.surface: An author has done well by having work translated into English.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is someone who writes, especially a copyist or a journalist.

clue.text: Doctor was there with daughter for turning point

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician was present with his daughter at a critical moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is a verb signalling the anagram: WAS THERE rearranged gives WATERSHE, then D is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed is a decisive moment of change, a synonym for turning point.

clue.text: Oil, perhaps, could be origin of thirst for war, OK?

indicators.note: could be suggests the following letters might form something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A question about whether petroleum might be what starts a thirst for conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil, perhaps' looks like petroleum but is an oil painting. 'origin of' gives T from thirst; with FOR, WAR and OK, 'could be' rearranges TFORWAROK.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil painting is one example of a work of art, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Animal I caught in dreadful trap

indicators.note: caught in tells us one piece is held inside the other
dreadful suggests the word trap is in a bad state, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature finds itself caught in a terrible snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges TRAP to TAPR, and 'caught in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir is a hoofed mammal with a short trunk, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Person looking round for pudding

definitions.meaning: someone who looks round is plump and rounded in shape
a British suet pudding rolled up with jam

explanation.definitionFit: Roly-poly describes a plump, round person and also names a rolled jam suet pudding.

clue.text: Author with regular book for horticultural class

parts.note: Thomas Hardy was an English novelist
an annual is a book published every year

explanation.surface: A writer with a yearly publication is filed under gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners classify plants such as cornflowers that survive cold and live one year as a hardy type of annual.

clue.text: Shoot down, say, casually

definitions.meaning: to bring down a bird or plane, as a gunner does
to mention something in passing, as with a hint or a name

explanation.definitionFit: Drop means to bring something down, and to let slip a remark casually, as in dropping a hint.

clue.text: Detective set-up that catches people offending quickly

definitions.text: Detective set-up that catches people offending quickly

parts.words: Detective set-up that catches people offending quickly
parts.note: sounds like a police sting, but the offence committed quickly is speeding and the detection is electronic

explanation.definitionFit: A speed check using radio-wave equipment to catch motorists exceeding the limit is a detecting set-up.

clue.text: Slow passage in old vessel on lake

indicators.note: on places the ship after the lake in this across answer

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason in Greek legend

explanation.surface: A leisurely voyage in an ancient ship across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction for a slow movement, so it names a slow passage of music.

clue.text: Nobody else could have written it

definitions.text: Nobody else could have written it

parts.words: Nobody else could have written it
parts.note: describes a book about a life that only its subject wrote

explanation.definitionFit: A book about one's own life written by oneself is by definition a work only its subject could pen.

clue.text: Nut on TV, .taking part of brutal king he admires

indicators.note: taking part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A television pundit who admires a cruel monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for head, and a talking head is a person on TV filmed from the shoulders up.

clue.text: As hard to swallow as potatoes, originally?

definitions.text: As hard to swallow as potatoes, originally?

parts.words: As hard to swallow as potatoes, originally?
parts.note: potatoes originally came to Europe from the distant Americas, while hard to swallow means unbelievable

explanation.definitionFit: Something incredible or implausible is said to be exaggerated beyond belief, a story stretched from a distance.

clue.text: Passed round thus to left, old port

indicators.note: passed round signals that the word is turned around

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: Something handed round to the left at a gathering, like vintage port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old port' looks like the fortified wine passed to the left at dinner, but 'old' is wordplay and 'port' is a harbour city. 'Passed round' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital is a long-established seaport on a fjord, so it is a port.

clue.text: Presidential residence, as represented in Spanish romantic movie

definitions.text: Presidential residence, as represented in Spanish
definitions.meaning: the White House rendered in Spanish
the 1942 Bogart and Bergman film is a famous wartime romance

explanation.definitionFit: The 1942 film with Bogart and Bergman is a classic romantic drama, and its title is Spanish for White House.

clue.text: Not dealing with a stated choice tribe put in

indicators.note: put in tells us the tribe is inserted into the other piece

parts.note: a voice is an expressed choice or say in a decision
Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: Refusing to engage with a choice offered to a tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoidance is the act of keeping away from something, and the noun phrase not dealing with names the same evasion.

clue.text: Flower new assistant pulled up — just like that!

indicators.note: pulled up in a down clue turns the letters upwards so they read backwards

parts.note: an aid is a helper or assistant
thus means in this way, just like that

explanation.surface: A fresh helper uproots a flower in one quick movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' reverses N + AID to give DIAN. 'just like that' was a catchphrase of British comic Tommy Cooper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dianthus is the genus of pinks and carnations, an example of a flower.

clue.text: With it, one gets admitted into one group 'of people

definitions.text: With it, one gets admitted into one group 'of people

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: gets admitted into says the first pieces go inside the next

parts.note: a nation is a group of people
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone joins a group of people by being given the secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets admitted into' places the second and third pieces after the first letter of the group, behind its N. The whole clue also describes the answer: admission into a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiation is the ceremony by which a person is admitted into a society or group.

clue.text: Use the Internet to' maintain one's standing on board?.

definitions.meaning: to ride waves standing on a board

explanation.definitionFit: Surf means to browse the web and also to ride waves standing on a surfboard.

clue.text: Conservative revolts creating a lot of emergencies

parts.note: rises means revolts, as in rises up

explanation.surface: A Tory uprising causes one emergency after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises is the plural of crisis, so many emergencies.

clue.text: Guy was actively involved in this tea garden section

definitions.text: Guy was actively involved in this

parts.note: gunpowder is a Chinese green tea rolled into pellets
a plot is a small piece of garden ground

explanation.surface: A man was busy in his tea garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes was one of the 1605 conspirators who tried to blow up Parliament; 'Guy' looks like any man.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Fawkes was a leading participant in the 1605 plan to blow up Parliament.

clue.text: Exceed rate of expenditure

definitions.meaning: money going out, the opposite of income

explanation.definitionFit: Outgo as a verb means to surpass, and as a noun means outlay or expenditure.

clue.text: Gardener's son pruned tree

indicators.note: pruned means cut back, so the end of the word is lopped off

parts.note: the abele is the white poplar tree

explanation.surface: A gardener's boy cuts back a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardener is Adam, who tended Eden; ABELE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel was a son of Adam, the first gardener in the Garden of Eden story.

clue.text: Tree for mast?

parts.note: suggests timber for a ship's mast, but mast also means the nuts that fall from certain trees

explanation.definitionFit: The fallen nuts of this tree are known as mast, so it is the tree that yields mast.

clue.text: Composer of minuets revised half of them

indicators.note: revised means the letters of minuets are reworked
half of takes the first two letters of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: A composer revised half of his minuets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges MINUETS as TUNESMI; 'half of' gives TH from them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunesmith is an informal word for someone who writes songs or music.

clue.text: Current occupant of seat in a pickle

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
an MP occupies a parliamentary seat

explanation.surface: The sitting member of Parliament finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a pickle' looks like the phrase for being in trouble; 'in' is a link and 'a pickle' is a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is an informal British word for a naughty child, as is an imp.

clue.text: Magnet school's head has style — on dole, unfortunately

indicators.note: on places the second part after the anagram in this across answer
unfortunately suggests the word dole has been knocked out of shape
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: tone means style or manner

explanation.surface: A school's headteacher has panache despite being out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges DOLE to LODE; 'head' gives S from school's. 'on dole' looks like one phrase but 'on' is the positional link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestone is naturally magnetic iron ore, a natural magnet.

clue.text: Good in blue, having excellent taste

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: blue means sad
pi, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: Feeling down but with a refined palate.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for good (pious) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means flavoursome, so a sapid food has excellent taste.
